domain: International Law / Criminal Justice / State Sovereignty
topic_summary: Analysis of the International Criminal Court's complementarity principle (Rome Statute Article 17), examining the structural tension between national sovereignty over criminal justice and international oversight of mass atrocity crimes. The principle establishes ICC jurisdiction as complementary to national courts but permits ICC intervention when states are unwilling or unable to prosecute genuinely.

key_entities: International Criminal Court (supranational court with jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, aggression)
State Parties to Rome Statute (signatories with treaty obligations but retained sovereignty claims)
National Courts (domestic judicial systems with primary jurisdiction under complementarity)
Office of the Prosecutor (ICC organ initiating investigations and assessing admissibility)
Victims of mass atrocity crimes (rights-holders under international humanitarian law)
Non-Party States (particularly USA, Russia, China - powerful states rejecting ICC jurisdiction)
key_tensions: State sovereignty vs international accountability (national courts as primary vs ICC as impunity guardian)
Procedural safeguards vs justice urgency (genuine investigation threshold vs timely intervention)

omegas.description: What constitutes 'genuine' investigation under Article 17(2)? Threshold interpretation determines whether most national proceedings satisfy complementarity or trigger ICC admissibility. This is the operational fulcrum where readings diverge most sharply.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + procedural_gatekeeping_mechanism analysis

omegas.description: Rome Statute lacks enforcement mechanism for non-cooperation. Does this absence convert international_oversight_reading into aspirational scaffold rather than operational constraint? Arrest warrant non-execution patterns suggest systematic extraction by powerful states.

Are hybrid tribunals (national courts + international judges/prosecutors) a third reading that transcends the binary? Or do they collapse into one reading when examined structurally? Sierra Leone Special Court and Cambodia ECCC may instantiate distinct constraint structure.
omegas.source: §3.1 Pairwise Test + Multi-Lens Scan (Comparative Criminal Justice Lens)

omegas.description: Aggression jurisdiction (activated 2018) alters complementarity dynamics by targeting state leadership directly. Does this shift the kernel itself, or merely expand the domain over which complementarity operates? Kampala amendments may have created kernel drift.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Multi-lens scan included sovereignty theory, international relations, comparative criminal procedure, and human rights lenses. commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Rome Statute Article 17 complementarity principle: ICC jurisdiction is complementary to national criminal jurisdictions, exercised only when states are unwilling or unable to investigate or prosecute genuinely
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Interpretive authority vested in ICC Pre-Trial Chamber for admissibility determinations; Office of the Prosecutor exercises prosecutorial discretion within Article 17 framework; state parties retain primary jurisdiction claim grounded in sovereignty

readings.commitment: Complementarity as sovereignty-protection mechanism; national courts presumptively adequate unless proven sham; ICC burden to demonstrate inadmissibility
readings.authority_grounding: Westphalian state sovereignty; treaty interpretation favoring retained jurisdiction (pacta sunt servanda applied to preserve signatory discretion)
readings.expected_structural_delta: High inadmissibility threshold; victims in states with weak-but-genuine proceedings fall outside ICC reach; state cooperation prioritized; beneficiaries are national judiciaries and sovereignty-maximizing states; victim set restricted to cases of complete judicial collapse

readings.commitment: Complementarity as accountability-trigger mechanism; ICC as guardian against impunity when states fail; 'unwilling or unable' interpreted broadly to capture victor's justice and elite immunity
readings.authority_grounding: International humanitarian law obligations (erga omnes); teleological treaty interpretation favoring object-and-purpose (Rome Statute Preamble: 'end impunity'); victims' rights prioritization
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low admissibility threshold; ICC intervenes when domestic proceedings lack independence or genuine intent; state cooperation demands intensify; beneficiaries are victims in complicit/failed states; victim set expands to include symbolic/sham prosecution scenarios

axiom_contradictions.basis: National_primacy reading holds sovereignty as lexically prior to accountability (states retain jurisdiction unless proven inadequate); international_oversight reading holds accountability as lexically prior to sovereignty (ICC authority presumed unless states prove adequacy). No coherent framework simultaneously treats sovereignty as presumptive gate-keeper and accountability as presumptive trigger—one must be default, the other exception.
